discovery: Electromagnetic metamaterials, negative refraction and transformation optics
motivation: Pendry showed that structured media of subwavelength resonators can realize effective permittivity and permeability unavailable in nature, including negative refraction and the 'perfect lens' that beats the diffraction limit. Smith turned this into experiment, demonstrating the first negative-index metamaterial (2000-2001) and, with Pendry, the first electromagnetic cloak (2006). In 2006 Pendry and, independently, Leonhardt founded transformation optics: coordinate transformations of Maxwell's equations, borrowing the language of general relativity, prescribe materials that steer light along any desired path. These ideas created an entire field whose reach goes well beyond optics, to acoustics, elastic and seismic waves, thermal transport, plasmonics, metasurfaces and flat optics now entering industry, and to laboratory analogues of curved spacetime and event horizons. This is a conceptual revolution in how we control waves, combining deep originality, clean experimental proof and real technological impact.
